dedupe_keys.name: ginom ai driven simulation of interdependent critical infrastructure risks and recovery

description: Ginom is a commercial platform that models the behaviour and interdependencies of infrastructure systems under different scenarios, predicts cascading risks and evaluates recovery strategies. The company describes three uses: analysing dependencies across systems to find vulnerabilities and plan recovery, managing crises in real time to keep services running, and training teams with realistic crisis simulations. It claims benefits such as fewer unplanned outages, shorter service interruptions and lower maintenance and insurance costs, and publishes webinars and articles on human factors and the cost of interrelated infrastructure failures. Its leadership includes a chairman described as a leader in infrastructure resilience and systemic risk and a chief executive with defence industry background. Coverage is not limited to one country. Format and access: a vendor-hosted platform offered through a pioneer programme with onboarding and training. Licence: proprietary, paid. Caveats: the website gives no technical documentation, validation or published case results, so its methods cannot be checked. It is an example of commercial digital twin tools for cascading failure and emergency response studies. Related catalogue records are the I2Sim infrastructure interdependencies simulator and the SmartResilience cascading effects simulator.
